name: Single-Arm Pec-Deck Flye
description: The single-arm pec-deck flye isolates one side of the chest at a time, allowing you to address muscular imbalances and achieve a deep stretch through the pectorals. By removing bilateral compensation, each side must work independently through the full arc of motion.

execution.starting_position: Sit on the pec-deck machine and grasp one handle with a single hand. Adjust the seat so your elbow is at shoulder height and your upper arm is parallel to the floor.
execution.setup_instructions: Set the machine to a weight you can control with one arm. Position the seat height so the shoulder joint is in line with the machine's pivot point.
steps: Step 1: Sit tall with your back firmly against the pad and feet flat on the floor.
Step 2: Grasp the single handle with one hand, arm slightly bent at the elbow.
Step 3: Drive the handle forward and across your body in a sweeping arc, squeezing the chest at peak contraction.
Step 4: Slowly return the handle to the starting position, allowing a controlled stretch across the chest.
Step 5: Complete all reps on one side before switching to the other.
execution.breathing_instructions: Exhale as you bring the handle forward through the arc. Inhale as you return to the stretched starting position.
common_mistakes: Rotating the torso to assist the movement
Using too much weight, reducing range of motion
Locking the elbow fully, stressing the joint
safety_considerations: Keep a slight bend in the elbow throughout
Do not force the arm behind the body's midline at the stretch
Adjust seat height carefully to protect the shoulder joint
execution.range_of_motion_guidance: Move through the full available arc without torso rotation. Allow a comfortable stretch at the start and a firm squeeze at the end.
coaching_cues: Arc the hand like you're hugging a tree
Keep the shoulder blade anchored to the pad
Squeeze and hold for a beat at peak contraction
